audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows were wrong in both layers — the chart was close to inverted against its own whys. Row 0 read Lillia though whys[0] says neither threatens a kill; rows 1-3 read Skill/Maokai/Maokai though whys[1..3] describe her kiting you off the wave every time; row 4 read Lillia though whys[4] says you win the all-in; row 5 read Maokai though whys[5] ends 'to even'.
audit.why: Her Blooming Blows move-speed stacks plus Swirlseed's slow beat a 13-14s Twisted Advance from 2 through 5. Level 6 is the genuine flip: Nature's Grasp is the first tool that catches her. First item stabilises to even; late you out-sustain her.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-5 set to Skill, Lillia, Lillia, Lillia, Maokai, Skill with ratings 5, 4, 4, 3, 7, 5 — matched full+content pairs in one atomic group, matching the packet chart and the mirror's re-scaled ratings inverted. Row 6 (Maokai 6/10) already correct. All seven phases[N].why rewritten so the full layer stops arguing against its own rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every stage was framed as a 'Blooming Blows cooldown window'. Blooming Blows is a 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s ability — it is never meaningfully down. The real spike is level 6.
audit.why: The thing you actually wait for is her move-speed stacks lapsing, and then Nature's Grasp at 6 (130s at rank 1). Her R is 150/130/110s and 1600 range — that is the long cooldown on her side, not her Q.
audit.corrected: Numbers and the level-6 flip written into tldr, winCon, phases[1].why, phases[3].why, phases[4].why, dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three factual errors in the content layer. (1) Slot names crossed: whys[1], spikes[0], early and wants.foe[0] call Blooming Blows her W — it is her Q; wants.foe[1] calls Swirlseed 'E (Watch Out!)' — Watch Out! Eep! is her W and E is Swirlseed. (2) 'her E dash' / 'E dashes' in whys[3], early and wants.you[0] — Lillia has NO dash anywhere in her kit. (3) 'E bounce' describes Swirlseed as a bounce; Riot says it rolls until it hits a wall or target.
audit.why: The dash claim is the damaging one: it tells you to wait for a cooldown that does not exist, when what you are actually waiting for is her Blooming Blows move-speed stacks decaying. That changes when you press W.
audit.corrected: Names and the no-dash correction written into whys[1], whys[3], spikes[0].text, early, wants.you[0], wants.foe[0], wants.foe[1], phases[3].why and report[5].t.

Levels 2-3 are genuinely hers: her W (Blooming Blows) move speed plus the E bounce let her chip you and slide out before your W (Twisted Advance) cooldown is back, and her passive DOT keeps ticking after she leaves. notes:
The biggest find on this page is that Lillia was given a dash she does not have. 'her E dash', 'E dashes', 'she's full of escapes' — none of that is in the kit; her only mobility is Blooming Blows' stacking move speed. That error made the advice actively wrong (wait for a cooldown that never comes, instead of waiting for stacks to decay). Corrected in every string long enough to edit.

Slot names were also crossed throughout the content layer: Blooming Blows called W, Swirlseed called 'Watch Out!'. Real mapping is Q Blooming Blows, W Watch Out! Eep!, E Swirlseed. Fixed where the band allowed. content.mid still says 'she could dance out of every Twisted Advance' — that phrasing survives because it does not assert a dash.

The mirror's open item, that Sap Magic acceleration undercuts the sustain claims in content.early/mid/wants.you[0], is on the lillia__maokai page. This page's early block is rewritten here for the naming errors and does not make that claim.

Champion-level kit-flag defect (sixth time): Maokai's Q carries a 'grounding' flag Riot's description does not support. Not asserted — and note the mirror agent DID write 'the grounding Q' into their tldr and report[0].t, which is exactly the fabrication this flag causes. That is a cross-page contradiction the user should know about.
